summary: Quarterly health check to review usage, costs, reliability, and roadmap. Zeta sees steady growth in embeddings and chat usage; primary concerns are 95th pct latency spikes during weekday evenings and higher-than-expected token costs. Discussed options: Dedicated vs hosted burst capacity, batching/quantization recommendations, and upcoming pilot for private deployment. Agreed on benchmarks and follow-ups.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Grant (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Zeta), Sofia Martinez (Zeta), Ethan Wu (Zeta), Priya Rao (Zeta)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for taking the time for the QBR really appreciate it. quick agenda - usage, costs, reliability, roadmap, and then action items. Olivia, wanna kick off with the usage numbers?
[00:20] Olivia Grant: yeah thanks Maya. so overall token usage is up about 28% q/q. chat sessions grew 34%, embeddings are up 40% driven by the new recommendation pipeline - that aligns with what you told us in the email liam. costs are up roughly 22% because of heavier long-form generation during peak hours and some retry traffic.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: yeah that's right; the rec sys kicked in more queries. also we pushed a new A/B where we keep longer context, so context length increased. that probably impacts cost.
[01:22] Ravi Patel: quick clarifying q - are those long contexts kept in-prefix cache or being resent each time? if you have the same prefix we can leverage KV caching; if not it increases per-token compute.
[01:38] Sofia Martinez: some are cached, but the way our service spawns ephemeral sessions means we lose some cache hits. priya's team is working on session stickiness but it's not in prod yet.
[01:55] Priya Rao: yep that's something on our backlog; we hit some infra constraints with our load balancer sticky session support.
[02:10] Maya Chen: okay makes sense. on the cost piece olivia you mentioned retries - any idea what's causing them?
[02:18] Olivia Grant: from metrics about 60% of retries look like client-side timeouts during 18:00-20:00 UTC, causing duplicate requests. Also a few 5xx's from the model endpoint during similar window but not systemic.
[02:40] Ethan Wu: to be clear our SRE flagged the 5xx cluster twice last month; we haven't correlated to Redwood logs yet, that's on our list.
[02:52] Maya Chen: fair. we'll make sure to send the logs link, riri - sorry ravi. ravi can run a more detailed tail of request ids with timestamps once you share the traces.
[03:05] Ravi Patel: yeah if you can give the trace export and a time range we'll run it through our incident correlate tool.
[03:14] Liam O'Connor: another thing - 95th percentile latency spikes are a customer complaint. during peak we see ~480ms p95 but sometimes it jumps to 1.2s which impacts UX.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: understood. quick notes on that - two levers: batching/autobatching and model variant routing. if you can accept slightly lower per-token accuracy we can route to a quantized faster variant at peak. also dedicated pools reduce contention.
[03:48] Sofia Martinez: we were wondering about dedicated - cost delta? right now hosted is simpler but if dedicated brings consistent latency maybe worth it.
[03:59] Olivia Grant: i'll put together formal cost comparisons but rough numbers show dedicated reserved capacity will increase fixed spend but reduce per-token variable cost; for sustained peak periods it often pays off. i'll share a break-even calc.
[04:15] Maya Chen: also worth noting we have burst capacity options - you can reserve baseline and allow burst to hosted. that can balance cost and latency.
[04:27] Ethan Wu: regarding private deployment - security reviews are moving along; legal asked for SOC2, KMS integration, and audit logs. do you have the SOC2 doc handy?
[04:40] Maya Chen: yes i'll send today's SOC2 attestation and our KMS integration guide and a private deployment checklist after the call.
[04:49] Priya Rao: for private we also need network diagrams and whether the control plane calls home.
[04:56] Maya Chen: control plane can be configured to use customer VPN/peered VPC, and audit logs are forwardable to your SIEM; i'll include details.
[05:07] Sofia Martinez: great. on reliability - any recommendations on retries/backoff? we implemented a 500ms client timeout but that seems aggressive.
[05:16] Ravi Patel: i'd recommend a sliding backoff up to 2s, and dedupe at the request id level to avoid duplicate generation costs. we can provide a library snippet.
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. can you also advise on batching configs? our traffic is bursty and we don't want added latency.
[05:36] Ravi Patel: sure - for bursty traffic we recommend adaptive batching with a 8-12ms aggregation window for chat and an opcode-level fast path for embeddings so embeddings go to a separate pool. that'll keep latency within SLO while gaining batching efficiency.
[05:52] Ethan Wu: earlier you mentioned quantization - does Redwood provide quantized model variants? what's the quality delta?
[05:59] Ravi Patel: yes we provide INT4/INT8 variants for many models; quality drop is model dependent. for the recommendation prompts you showed, INT8 had negligible impact in our evals; for long-form creative generation INT4 showed some degeneration. we can run a prompt-set eval on your prompts as part of the pilot.
[06:18] Sofia Martinez: please do that - we'd like a regression matrix.
[06:22] Olivia Grant: i'll coordinate that, include a small eval harness and the results in the cost report.
[06:28] Maya Chen: good. quick pause - any outstanding compliance blockers?
[06:33] Priya Rao: legal wants a KMS flow and key custody options (bring-your-own-key). is that available?
[06:39] Maya Chen: yes BYOK is supported via KMS integrations; customer keys can be enforced for private deployments. i'll include specifics in the doc.
[06:48] Liam O'Connor: timeline question - if we decide to pilot private deployment, how long to stand up? we are targeting end of Q2 if possible.
[06:58] Ravi Patel: typical private deployment with a small pilot (one region, limited models) is 4-6 weeks for infra + validation; if your infra team is ready we can compress some steps.
[07:09] Sofia Martinez: okay that fits our internal timeline.
[07:12] Maya Chen: great - let's talk benchmarks. liam, can you share representative peak-hour traces?
[07:18] Liam O'Connor: yes we'll export a sample of two weekdays and one weekend peak.
[07:23] Ravi Patel: perfect. i'll run a 500-concurrent synthetic test that mirrors your request distribution and share p50/p95/p99 and token throughput.
[07:32] Ethan Wu: will that include cold-start behaviors? we saw some cold kv cache misses early in the day.
[07:38] Ravi Patel: yep i'll run both warm and cold scenarios. cold includes 0 cache priming and warm simulates realistic cache hit rates.
[07:47] Olivia Grant: on the cost side, a few practical recommendations: 1) enable prefix/KV caching where possible, 2) use quantized variants during non-critical flows, 3) enable dedupe for retries, 4) consider reserved baseline for nightly batch jobs.
[08:02] Sofia Martinez: for recommendation batch jobs, we can also move some work offline to embeddings-only pipelines to reduce real-time token spend.
[08:11] Ravi Patel: exactly - embeddings are cheaper per unit for vectorization workloads and can be sharded to a CPU pool if latency requirements are looser.
[08:20] Liam O'Connor: quick question - you mentioned model routing by policy earlier. can we route by customer segment and latency SLO?
[08:28] Maya Chen: yes policy routing supports attributes like customer segment, route latency SLO, and cost budget. you can pin premium clients to dedicated low-latency pool and route others to cost-optimized variants.
[08:40] Ethan Wu: that capability would help our monetization plan. we need an estimate for the per-segment cost delta.
[08:46] Olivia Grant: i'll include a per-segment back-of-envelope in the cost report.
[08:51] Priya Rao: any limitations on data residency? some of our EU customers require all inference to stay in eu-west-1.
[08:58] Maya Chen: we support region pinning for model serving and private deployments can be constrained to specific regions; we'll document data residency and logging flows.
[09:07] Sofia Martinez: thanks. we're also tracking a couple of small reliability incidents - can you share endpoint-level traces and the request ids we gave you last time?
[09:17] Ravi Patel: we have those, we'll correlate and send a root-cause summary. some were due to autoscaling with cold replicas, which we've improved with a warmed-replica config.
[09:30] Maya Chen: okay wrapping to next steps. recapping: Ravi to run synthetic benchmarks (500 concurrent) and share results by 2026-04-02; Olivia to send cost reconciliation and batching/quant recommendations by 2026-04-01; Maya to send SOC2/KMS/private deployment docs by 2026-03-30; Sofia to share peak traces by 2026-03-29.
[09:52] Liam O'Connor: cool. can we also get a short deck for execs summarizing recommended architecture and expected cost delta?
[09:58] Maya Chen: yes i'll put together a 2-page exec summary and cc ravi and olivia.
[10:05] Ethan Wu: one last item - pilot scope. can we define pilot as: 2 models (chat + rec embeddings), 1 region, traffic mirror at 10% for 2 weeks?
[10:15] Ravi Patel: that scope is doable. we'll need your infra access for logs and a service account for the duration.
[10:23] Sofia Martinez: we'll provision that if we decide to proceed after the benchmark.
[10:27] Maya Chen: perfect. any final questions?
[10:31] Priya Rao: no final questions. thanks everyone.
[10:34] Maya Chen: thanks all - we'll follow-up with the artifacts and set the pilot kickoff tentatively week of 2026-04-06. bye.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (names slightly off), timestamps are approximate and inserted every few minutes for navigation. Action items and next steps were confirmed verbally at the end of the call.
